 Women's Soccer to Open Patriot League Tournament Play with Wednesday Matinee versus Loyola
 Mids defeated the Greyhounds in regular season finale, 2-1
 Story Links
 Live Video 
 Live Stats 
 Game Notes 
 ANNAPOLIS, Md. - All of the reps put in during the offseason, miles run during the non-conference and strategy fine-tuned during conference play culminates this week for the Navy women's soccer team with action in the 2026 Patriot League Tournament. After going 7-3-1 versus non-conference foes, the Mids (14-4-2) dropped the first game of Patriot League play to Boston University on Sept. 19, but has since gone undefeated (7-0-1) to secure the top seed in the year-end league tournament. First up in Navy's road to Patriot League Championship number six is a semifinal matchup with the sixth-seeded Loyola Greyhounds (4-4-10) at 12 p.m. in Annapolis. The winner of Wednesday's contest will advance to the Patriot League Finals that will be hosted at the highest remaining seed on Sunday, Nov. 15; the final four clubs still alive for the title are No. 1 Navy, No. 2 Army, No. 4 Boston University and No. 6 Loyola.
In a random scheduling oddity, Wednesday's playoff meeting will be rematch from just one week prior when Navy knocked off Loyola on Nov. 4 by a score of 2-1 to clinch a share of the Patriot League regular season title. This will be the fourth time in the 34-year history of the Navy Women's Soccer that the Mids will face the same opponent in back-to-back games; the regular season finale and the postseason opener ... 1995 against Bucknell (Loss, Win); 2008 versus Colgate (Win, Win) and 2019 against Loyola (Tie ,Tie-advanced on PKs).
The Navy-Loyola contest will have live stats provided online, as well as an ESPN+ broadcast.  ESPN+ is a subscription-based streaming service that requires patrons to sign-up for monthly or yearly plans prior to tuning into the contest. 
 Navy in the Patriot League Tournament 
Wednesday will begin the Mids' 27th trip in the Patriot League Tournament out of 33 eligible seasons in program history ... All-time, the Mids are 20-21-2 and have finished as champions in 2003, 2006, 2007, 2019 and 2020-21 ... Navy is 13-9-1 all-time in 23 Patriot League semifinal competitions; the program was last in a semifinal contest against Loyola on April 14, 2021 as part of the COVID-impacted playoff tournament ... This will be the eighth Patriot League Tournament that the Mids will enter as the number one seed; most recently they were the top seed of the 2019 event, that saw them open at home against Loyola on Nov. 8, 2019 ... All-time, Navy is 7-0 in Patriot League semifinal games as the number one seed ... Both times that Navy opened a Patriot League Tournament with a matchup with Loyola (2019 and 2021), they won and went on to win the championship in the ensuing game.
 Navy vs. Loyola 
In a series that dates back to the first-ever NCAA Division I game for Navy on Sept. 4, 1993, the Mids are 13-5-5 all-time against the Greyhounds ... After dropping the first two games of the series in 1993 and 1994, Navy has fallen to Loyola just three times in the past 29 years; a Sept. 24, 2016 meeting by a score of 2-1 in double overtime before getting nipped 1-0 in games during the 2022 and 2023 regular season contest ... Since Loyola joined the Patriot League in 2013, Navy is 7-3-4 over 14 regular season meetings ... The Mids also hold a 2-0-1 advantage in three Patriot League Tournament matchups: a 4-1 win on Nov. 4, 2014, a 1-1 tie on Nov. 8, 2019 (Navy advanced on PKs) and a 1-0 victory on April 14, 2021 (all three games were played in Annapolis) ... The teams have met 14 times in Annapolis with the Mids posting an 9-2-3 mark.
 Last 5 Matchups 
In the last five meetings dating back to 2022, the series is knotted at 2-2-1 with each team recording seven goals each.
    Nov. 4, 2026 (H): Navy 2 - Loyola 1
    Oct. 29, 2025 (A): Navy 1 - Loyola 1
    Sept. 25, 2024 (H): Navy 4 - Loyola 3
    Sept. 20, 2023 (A): Loyola 1 - Navy 0
    Sept. 21, 2022 (H): Loyola 1 - Navy 0

 Last Time Out: Wednesday, Nov. 4 versus Loyola in Annapolis  
Playing the last game of the entire 2026 Patriot League regular season schedule, the Navy women's soccer team came in laser-focused at the one task at hand, win and secure home field advantage throughout the Patriot League Tournament. Coming into the day in second place, one game behind Army, Navy got the break it needed when Holy Cross knocked off the previously undefeated Black Knights 2-1. With that result finalized before the kickoff in Annapolis, the attention of the entire league was on the pitch at the Glenn Warner Soccer Facility with Wednesday night's matchup between Navy and Loyola. After 90 minutes of heart-pounding ultra-competitive action the host Midshipmen (14-4-2, 7-1-1 PL) were victorious by a score of 2-1 over the Greyhounds (3-4-10, 3-3-3 PL).
With all the pressure built into the contest, it was a freshman, Sophia Ryan , who was star of the game with her first career two-goal performance. Both of Ryan's goals, the first in the seventh minute and game-winner in the 79th were assisted upon by Chiara Cosenza  with Jessica Black adding a secondary assist on the game-winning tally.
Invigorated by the news of Army's loss opening the door for a shot at a share of the Patriot League Regular Season Championship and the number one overall seed in the upcoming conference tournament, Navy came out with a purpose. That purpose was to get ahead and hold off a talented Loyola squad. Ryan made sure that first goal was attained as she worked a give-and-go with Cosenza to put her in position for a high-arching shot that found the far upper-90 of the goal just 6:12 into the contest.
Unfortunately for the Mids and their home fans, that lead was short-lived as a little over 12 minutes later, Betzael Contreras knotted the contest at 1-1 for the Greyhounds with a rocket of a shot off a loose bouncing ball following a free kick into the box.
The action inside the attacking thirds slowed down following that game-tying tally as the teams combined for just three total shots the final 33 minutes of the half, all coming from Navy. 
Coming out of the locker room tied at 1-1 both teams knew that to improve their playoff seeding they would need to win so finding that go-ahead goal would be paramount. The Greyhounds almost succeeding in that quest as 63 seconds into the second half, Taryn Buckley picked off a pass in the Mids' defensive third and dribbled in towards the goal before Natasha Stramrood  sprinted off her line and corralled the ball as Buckley was just releasing her shot. 
Following that play at 46:03, Loyola's offense was held completely at bay by Navy as the visitors were unable to record even one shot for the final 43-plus minutes. With their defense leading the way, things began to open up slightly for the Mids' offense as the hosts recorded a pair of shots and three corner kicks within the next 30 minutes.
The in-roads that Navy was making finally paid off at 78:07 when Black crossed the ball in from the left wing to Cosenza, who deftly evaded a Loyola defender and drew its goalkeeper out of the crease before laying off a pass to Ryan, who didn't blink and smashed her shot into the back of the gaping net.
Back ahead by one, Navy successfully ran out the final 11:53 on the clock to seal the victory and more importantly clinch the number one seed in the Patriot League Tournament.
For the game, Navy out-shot Loyola, 9-2 with a 4-2 edge in shots on goal. The Mids also held an 8-1 advantage in corner kick opportunities.
 Parking / Shuttle 
Fans are reminded that the general public does not have access to drive their vehicles on to the U.S. Naval Academy. Fans may park at Navy-Marine Corps Memorial Stadium for a fee and take a shuttle that will run every 10 minutes starting one hour before the game and will continue running until one hour after the game is completed. Enter Gate 5 off Taylor Ave. to park at the stadium. Fans 18 and over need a government-issued photo ID. 
**Starting May 7, 2025, in accordance with The Real ID Act of 2005, visitors entering through the Pedestrian Gate 1 Visitor Control Center or accessing the USNA through the fan shuttle bus for a game should be prepared to present a REAL ID-compliant driver's license, U.S. Passport, enhanced state-issued ID, or another acceptable form of identification, to access federal facilities.  Foreign passports are NOT permitted for general access.
